title: Skeleton Rigging Joint Hierarchy Viewer
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive skeleton rigging joint hierarchy viewer.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x1a1a2e) with a subtle grid floor (20x20, color 0x333355) at y=0.
- Perspective camera at position (0, 5, 12), looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) from (5, 10, 5).
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.

## Skeleton Hierarchy
- Build a humanoid skeleton hierarchy using Three.js Bone objects with the following structure:
  - Root (hip) at (0, 4, 0)
    - Spine at relative (0, 1.2, 0)
      - Chest at relative (0, 1.2, 0)
        - Head at relative (0, 1.0, 0)
        - LeftShoulder at relative (-0.8, 0.8, 0)
          - LeftElbow at relative (-1.2, 0, 0)
            - LeftHand at relative (-1.0, 0, 0)
        - RightShoulder at relative (0.8, 0.8, 0)
          - RightElbow at relative (1.2, 0, 0)
            - RightHand at relative (1.0, 0, 0)
    - LeftHip at relative (-0.5, -0.2, 0)
      - LeftKnee at relative (0, -1.8, 0)
        - LeftFoot at relative (0, -1.8, 0)
    - RightHip at relative (0.5, -0.2, 0)
      - RightKnee at relative (0, -1.8, 0)
        - RightFoot at relative (0, -1.8, 0)
- Create a Three.js Skeleton from these bones.
- Visualize each joint as a small sphere (radius 0.15, 0x00ffaa emissive material).
- Connect parent-child joints with cylinder or line segments (color 0x4488ff, linewidth or thin cylinders).

## Joint Selection & Interaction
- Clicking on a joint sphere via raycasting selects it. The selected joint turns yellow (0xffff00). Only one joint selected at a time.
- When a joint is selected, display its name, world position (x,y,z), local rotation (Euler degrees), and depth in hierarchy in an info panel (top-right DOM overlay, styled dark semi-transparent box).
- Keyboard controls when a joint is selected:
  - 'X' key: rotate selected joint +15 degrees around local X axis
  - 'Y' key: rotate selected joint +15 degrees around local Y axis
  - 'Z' key: rotate selected joint +15 degrees around local Z axis
  - 'R' key: reset selected joint rotation to (0,0,0)
  - 'Space' key: deselect current joint

## Hierarchy Tree Panel
- On the left side, render a DOM-based collapsible tree view showing the bone hierarchy.
- Each node shows the bone name. Clicking a tree node selects that joint (same as clicking the 3D sphere).
- The currently selected joint's tree node should be highlighted (bright text or background).

## Animation Pose Presets
- Add 3 buttons at the bottom of the screen: 'T-Pose', 'A-Pose', 'Wave Pose'.
  - T-Pose: all rotations reset to 0 (default).
  - A-Pose: shoulders rotated -30 degrees on Z axis (arms angled down).
  - Wave Pose: RightShoulder Z=-90deg, RightElbow X=45deg (arm raised and bent).
- Applying a pose should animate smoothly over 0.5 seconds using interpolation.
- Track the current pose name.

## Bone Chain Length Display
- When a joint is selected, compute and display the total chain length from root to that joint (sum of distances between consecutive joints in the chain). Show this in the info panel.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
  - totalBones: number (total bone count, should be 15)
  - selectedJoint: string|null (name of selected joint or null)
  - selectedJointDepth: number (depth in hierarchy, root=0)
  - selectedJointWorldPos: {x, y, z} (world position of selected joint)
  - selectedJointLocalRot: {x, y, z} (local Euler rotation in degrees)
  - currentPose: string ('t-pose'|'a-pose'|'wave-pose'|'custom')
  - chainLength: number (chain length from root to selected joint, 0 if none selected)
  - hierarchyExpanded: boolean (whether tree panel is visible)
  - boneNames: string[] (array of all bone names in depth-first order)
  - animating: boolean (true while pose transition is in progress)
  - jointRotationCount: number (total number of manual rotations applied via keyboard)
- Update state every frame.

## Additional
- Add a toggle button 'Toggle Hierarchy' that shows/hides the tree panel, updating hierarchyExpanded.
- Ensure all world positions are updated after rotations (call updateMatrixWorld).
- The skeleton visualization (spheres and lines) must update in real-time as bones rotate.
physics_constraints: Joint rotations must propagate correctly through the hierarchy (child joints inherit parent transforms). Chain length calculations must be geometrically accurate based on actual world positions. Pose interpolation must complete in approximately 0.5 seconds. All world positions must be NaN-free and finite.
